column1: # The Wiz trust ledger: the trusted base of lib/ (and the axiom-free examples).
# One row per source of trust, tab-separated:
#   module, declaration, item, reason, owner, review
# `item` is the wording of `#print axioms`: `axiom X`, `native f := g` for
# implemented_by, `native T := mk/get` for a repr registration, `native_refl
# X.native✝` (compiled evaluation, the analogue of Lean's native_decide), `smt
# `builtin inline` (a compiler hint) and `builtin int` (how values print) are not
# Every row needs a non-empty reason, owner and review date (YYYY-MM-DD); a row
# is expired when its review date is before today. Rows from the migration still
# say `legacy: pre-gate baseline; not individually reviewed` and owner
# `unassigned`: they are only counted (and --strict-legacy fails on them).
# A new source fails the `native` group and scripts/trust-ledger.sh --check; add a

compiled `InternTable.find` calls `InternTable.findNative` (`wiz_itab_find`): the C function computes the definition (see its row); the `=natives` group runs the same program under the model and the natives, C and LLVM, so a disagreement fails
`wiz_itab_find(wiz_val, wiz_val) -> wiz_val`: returns a string's id as `Option U32` (hashed by code points), which is `InternTable.find = indexL`

marshals `InternTable.findNative` as `wiz_itab_find(wiz_val, wiz_val) -> wiz_val`: the kind string `ww→w` passes w→wiz_val (as it is), w→wiz_val (as it is); result w→wiz_val (as it is); the arity and C types agree with the prototype exactly, each kind passed as the C type the glue uses for it (a Nat as uint64_t through wiz_in_nat)

compiled `InternTable.intern` calls `InternTable.internNative` (`wiz_itab_intern`): the C function computes the definition (see its row); the `=natives` group runs the same program under the model and the natives, C and LLVM, so a disagreement fails

`wiz_itab_intern(wiz_val, wiz_val) -> wiz_val`: returns the table with the string and the string's id (a new id, the old count, when new; it aborts at the model's 2^32 ids), which is `InternTable.intern`

marshals `InternTable.internNative` as `wiz_itab_intern(wiz_val, wiz_val) -> wiz_val`: the kind string `ww→w` passes w→wiz_val (as it is), w→wiz_val (as it is); result w→wiz_val (as it is); the arity and C types agree with the prototype exactly, each kind passed as the C type the glue uses for it (a Nat as uint64_t through wiz_in_nat)

compiled `InternTable.lookup` calls `InternTable.lookupNative` (`wiz_itab_lookup`): the C function computes the definition (see its row); the `=natives` group runs the same program under the model and the natives, C and LLVM, so a disagreement fails
`wiz_itab_lookup(wiz_val, wiz_val) -> wiz_val`: returns the string with an id, or the empty string (out of range), which is `InternTable.lookup`

marshals `InternTable.lookupNative` as `wiz_itab_lookup(wiz_val, wiz_val) -> wiz_val`: the kind string `ww→w` passes w→wiz_val (as it is), w→wiz_val (as it is); result w→wiz_val (as it is); the arity and C types agree with the prototype exactly, each kind passed as the C type the glue uses for it (a Nat as uint64_t through wiz_in_nat)

compiled `InternTable.mk` is the pair `InternTable.ofListNative`/`InternTable.toListNative` (`wiz_itab_of_list`, `wiz_itab_to_list`): the constructor and field of the model's single-field representation, both checked against the C functions; the `=natives` group runs the model and the natives, C and LLVM
`wiz_itab_of_list(wiz_val) -> wiz_val`: builds the hash index over the distinct strings in order, giving each id its index, which is the model's `mk strs`

marshals `InternTable.ofListNative` as `wiz_itab_of_list(wiz_val) -> wiz_val`: the kind string `w→w` passes w→wiz_val (as it is); result w→wiz_val (as it is); the arity and C types agree with the prototype exactly, each kind passed as the C type the glue uses for it (a Nat as uint64_t through wiz_in_nat)

`wiz_itab_to_list(wiz_val) -> wiz_val`: returns the strings by id, the model's field
